name: The Elunad

identity.symbol: A silver hoofprint beneath a crescent moon
identity.public_perception: Venerated as road-blessers, feared as spirit-guides, often misunderstood. Sought after as guides, but resented when they refuse to lead. True Elunad rarely declare themselves openly — false bearers of their tokens have brought tragedy, and the order is wary as a result.

goals.primary: To connect and preserve roads and isolated enclaves — keeping the paths between what remains of civilization passable and protected.
secondary: Reopen old roads and aid pilgrims on the five Irkali pilgrimage routes.
Interpret omens at crossroads and preserve fragments of pre-Silence travel magic.
Guard the five sacred sites where the new gods first emerged.
goals.hidden_agenda: Some Elunad believe they are charting the forgotten geometry of the gods — that the roads, fords, and shrines they maintain form a pattern, and they are preparing the way for something still unknown.

philosophy.summary: The Elunad are heirs by bequest, not blood, to an ancient order of imperial emissaries and road-guardians. Their lineage traces through tokens, not families — each true Elunad carries a handcrafted object passed from mentor to student back to the Old Empire itself. Few remain. They carry the memory of an unbroken road.
methods: Travel alone or in silent pairs — never in numbers.
Communicate through bells, path-marking sigils, and silent gestures.
Only draw steel when pilgrims or roads are directly threatened.
Authenticate identity through ancestral tokens — antler-wrapped stone, etched iron, silver knot — each bearing unmistakable markings of the order.
limits: Will not authenticate false token-bearers — the consequences have been too severe.

position.territory: Roads, fords, mountain passes, and borderlands — never cities. The five Irkali pilgrimage routes are their primary responsibility.
position.active_since: Founded when the first shrines to Isarna were raised along the ruined pilgrim roads after the Fall. Their practices preserve fragments of pre-Silence travel magic.

alliances.nature: Occasional alignment around shared border-keeping. Neither answers to the other.
The Elunad guard Isarna's pilgrimage routes and waystone network. Isarnan clergy and dream-guides are among their most reliable contacts.

rivals.nature: Woodwoses, humanoids, and usurpers of roads are ongoing threats to the routes the Elunad protect.
Those who exploit roads for private gain are a persistent enemy — not always violent, but always opposed.

needs: Roads and fords left passable and uncontrolled.
Communities that venerate the pilgrimage routes and waystones.
Students willing to accept the token and the full weight of the lineage.
provides: Safe passage and guidance across roads, fords, and borderlands.
Interpretation of omens and crossroads signs.
Maintenance of the five Irkali pilgrimage routes and their sacred sites.
Messengers and liaisons across isolated enclaves.

pilgrimage-routes.name: The Five Irkali Routes
pilgrimage-routes.role: The five sacred pilgrimage roads connecting the sites where the new gods first emerged after the Silence. Each is fraught with peril. The Elunad maintain and guard them.
pilgrimage-routes.notes: These are the Elunad's primary operational responsibility. Their practices preserve fragments of pre-Silence travel magic used to keep the routes passable.

waystone-network.name: Waystone Network
waystone-network.role: Shrines and waystones maintained along roads and at crossroads. Isarnan observance points. Provide structure for the Elunad's silent communication network.
waystone-network.notes: The Waystone of Isarna west of Tagmira is one such node — Taziri Nkhaleb stops here for offering (bread, silver thread) on her caravan routes. Her late husband Irven was Elunad, killed by lizard-men 8 years ago.

token-lineages.name: Token Lineages
token-lineages.role: The chain of mentorship through which the order perpetuates itself. Each token traces lineage to the Old Empire. False bearers have brought tragedy; authentication is serious business.
token-lineages.notes: Many tokens have been lost. The order is smaller than it once was. No central registry exists — lineage is known only to those within it.

dm_notes: Taziri Nkhaleb's late husband Irven was Elunad — killed by lizard-men 8 years ago. This is a live connection to the faction for the party. The waystone west of Tagmira is a natural scene transition point. The hidden geometry thread — that the road network forms a divine pattern — is a long-term revelation available if the party engages deeply with the Elunad. The five Irkali sacred sites are each a potential adventure location. Matt G.'s ranger character is a member; his token lineage is undeveloped.
